task.title: Runtime validation gate: apply P30 acceptance rules and guardrails with deterministic fallback on rejection
task.objective: Extract the inline guardrail logic currently embedded in appraisal_router.py into a dedicated, standalone validation gate module (back/app/llm/validation_gate.py). The gate takes a ShadowRunResult, a deterministic baseline AppraisalOutput, and a ComparisonVerdict, and returns a structured GateDecision that records whether the LLM output is accepted or rejected, the rejection reason, and which failure mode category triggered the rejection. The router is then updated to call the gate instead of duplicating guardrail logic inline. The gate enforces all BLOCKING guardrail policies defined in failure_taxonomy.py: STRUCTURAL_FAIL verdict triggers rejection, and a valence deviation with severity=severe triggers rejection.
task.exact_scope: One new module: back/app/llm/validation_gate.py. One new test file: back/tests/test_p31_t2_validation_gate.py. Minimal update to back/app/llm/appraisal_router.py to delegate guardrail decisions to the gate rather than evaluating them inline — no other behavioural changes to the router. No other files are modified. The gate is a pure function that accepts structured inputs and returns a structured GateDecision. It never calls the LLM, writes state, or raises to its caller.
acceptance_criteria: back/app/llm/validation_gate.py exists and is importable with no side effects

validation_gate.py exports a GateDecision model with fields: accepted (bool), rejection_reason (Optional[str] — None when accepted=True), failure_category (Optional[FailureModeCategory] — None when accepted=True)
validation_gate.py exports a public function evaluate(shadow_result: ShadowRunResult, deterministic_baseline: AppraisalOutput, verdict: Optional[ComparisonVerdict]) -> GateDecision

When the shadow runner already fell back (shadow_result.llm_used=False), evaluate() returns accepted=False with failure_category=LLM_CONNECTION_FAILURE or LLM_PARSE_FAILURE as appropriate, and rejection_reason matching the shadow_result.failure_reason
When the verdict is None (deferred tick), evaluate() returns accepted=True — the gate does not block deterministic-only outputs

When the verdict has overall=STRUCTURAL_FAIL, evaluate() returns accepted=False with failure_category=ZERO_ABSORPTION_OVERRIDE (or the most specific BLOCKING category applicable) and a non-None rejection_reason
When the verdict has a FieldDeviation on valence with severity=severe, evaluate() returns accepted=False with failure_category=VALENCE_SIGN_FLIP and a non-None rejection_reason
When the verdict is SEMANTIC_PASS, evaluate() returns accepted=True
When the verdict is SEMANTIC_DEGRADED with no severe valence deviation and no structural failures, evaluate() returns accepted=True

appraisal_router.py is updated to call validation_gate.evaluate() instead of evaluating guardrail conditions inline — the RouterResult fields and routing behaviour are identical to the pre-update behaviour
back/tests/test_p31_t2_validation_gate.py exists and all tests in it pass under: cd back && python3 -m pytest tests/test_p31_t2_validation_gate.py -v
All previously passing tests continue to pass (no regression): cd back && python3 -m pytest tests/ -v

The router behavioural contract (routing rules, fallback triggers, RouterResult shape) must be preserved exactly — only the internal implementation of guardrail evaluation changes

## Round-0043 Summary — **PASSED**

**Task:** P31-T2 — Runtime validation gate with deterministic fallback on rejection

### What was built
1. **`back/app/llm/validation_gate.py`** (new) — A pure `evaluate()` function returning a `GateDecision` Pydantic model that classifies each LLM appraisal result as accepted or rejected. Enforces all BLOCKING guardrail policies:

   - Severe valence deviation → rejected with `VALENCE_SIGN_FLIP`
   - `SEMANTIC_PASS` / `SEMANTIC_DEGRADED` (no severe valence) → accepted

- No forbidden files modified
- No regressions
